children: Skybridge Capital
founder
Anthony Scaramucci
once warned that ego and pride can cloud judgment and should be kept out of decision-making.
How Scaramucci Learned a ‘Big Lesson’
Speaking to journalist
Katie Curic
on Sept. 24, Scaramucci reflected on a “colossal” mistake he regrets to this day.
The financier recalled campaigning for President
Donald Trump
in the 2016 election and later being named to the 16-person Executive Committee of the Presidential Transition Team.
Scaramucci said he held a negative opinion of
Steve Bannon
, then the White House chief strategist, and shared that view with Trump.
Trump then invited him to join the administration, an offer Scaramucci recounts his mentor strongly advised against.
“And this is a big lesson for people listening. You can’t put your pride and your ego into your decision-making,” said the 62-year old hedge fund manager.
Scaramucci served as White House Communications Director but was fired after just 11 days after a
, in which he vulgarized Bannon’s efforts to build a personal media brand off the strength of the president.
“You got to be very careful with your ego in your personal relationships, your business relationships, your ambition,” he added.
A Tale of Success and Setbacks
Before launching SkyBridge Capital in 2005, Scaramucci had co-founded
Oscar Capital Management
, an investment firm that was sold to
Neuberger Berman
He was fired from
Goldman Sachs
early in his career because management felt he was performing poorly, before being rehired weeks later.
Scaramucci has
, including "Solana Rising: Investing in the Fast Lane of Crypto" and "The Little Book of Bitcoin." His wealth is estimated at $150 million, according to Celebrity Net Worth.
Scaramucci previously revealed that over 70% of his net worth is invested in
Bitcoin
